# Coaching Philosophy - Lamar Cochran

> Two junior seasons in Canada and seven SHL seasons taught me one thing: the bench wins games the staff prepared for, not the games we improvised through.

## Core principles

1. **On-ice work first.** Every meeting answers a practice question or it doesn't happen.
2. **Layered cues.** Players hear one message from me, the same message phrased differently from Nils, and the same idea reinforced by the video room. Three angles on one thought.
3. **Show, then tell.** Drill demo before whistle, never after.
4. **Special teams are character.** Penalty kill is where you find out who reads the play.
5. **The room owns the result.** Win or lose, the locker room is the first audience for the truth.

## Sources I keep returning to

- Tommy Svensson's bench notebooks (loaned in 2023, returned 2024 with annotations)
- Mike Babcock's '93 World Juniors prep doc (via the federation diploma archive)
- The Brynas J20 1998 systems binder Nils tracked down

## Notes on adapting NA structure to Nordic ice

The wider sheet doesn't reward the same forecheck pressure. F1-F2 sortie still works as a trigger but the F3 must read the weak-side reload before committing. (See [[brynas-h2h-week-of-2027-01-25]].)

# 2026-27 Season Principles

Quick reference. Updated when the bench learns something.

## Game plan defaults

- **Forecheck:** F1-F2 sortie, F3 reads weak side.
- **D-zone coverage:** Man-on-puck low, swing-back high if half-wall releases.
- **Power play:** 1-3-1 with right-side option; Oskar's wall feed when the seam opens.
- **Penalty kill:** Diamond, weak-side D walks the blue if the half-wall stalls.

## Line decisions

- Heavy middle minutes for the captain rotation against top six.
- Third-pair starts when video shows a forecheck susceptible to wall-out.
- Special-teams ratios re-baseline every fourth game.

## Things I will not do

- Talk lineups outside the staff allowlist.
- Share medical info beyond cleared / not-cleared.
- Trade Tommy's mentor calls for media windows.

# Brynas J20 H2H - week of 2027-01-25

Three head-to-head matchups this season; this is matchup four.

## Their tendencies

- F1-F2 sortie, F3 stalls weak side waiting for reload.
- PP heavy on the right-side wall; their #11 reads our half-wall pressure.
- PK diamond collapses on the bumper; opens the seam between the dots.

## Our adjustments

- Third-pair starts: Oskar gets heavy middle minutes; right-side stride watch from the morning skate.
- Second period: switch PP entry from outside-in to a delayed quick-up.
- PK: walk our weak-side D to the blue every fourth shift to break their stall.

> Cross with [[oskar-stride-watch-2027-01-23]] and the Notion line-combinations cut. If the new cut moves Oskar off the third pair, the heavy-middle-minutes call still holds.

# Oskar Stride Watch - morning skate 2027-01-23

Quick from the 9am skate. Captured here before it leaves my head.

## Observation

- Right-side stride length looked tighter on the push during the wall-out drill.
- Half-step shorter on the push, not big.
- Compare with last two video sessions: same look on the second clip of the December tape; not flagged at the time.
- Compare with the most recent Strand follow-up: cleared to play; no flags raised.

## Action

- Pin a watch-list flag to the Oskar Ek Notion development page so the line decisions for the next home game surface this before the locker room walk-in.
- Cross-link this note from [[brynas-h2h-week-of-2027-01-25]].

# Post-Brynas voice memo - second-period special teams

The diamond stall happened twice in the first. We walked our weak-side D to the blue on shift seven of the second and the bumper opened up. Got the look we wanted, didn't bury it.

## Worth remembering

- Walking the weak-side D early breaks the diamond stall consistently.
- The bumper window opens for about two seconds; you have to feed the seam, not the wall.
- Oskar's third-rotation read on heavy middle minutes worked - two five-on-five chances against, no defensive lapses.

## Next time

- Build a pre-period cue: when their PK collapses on the bumper, the walk goes on the second whistle, not the third.
